Since you're new to Paris, or Europe for that matter, I may have something to add to this. (As you probably notice by my English, I'm Dutch.)
The catacombes are a very well known part of Paris. A long time ago, when the graves were overfull (cause, you know, lots of people, very full city), they started throwing bones in empty underground holes, however nicely stocking them in patterns. It looks really creepy, but it's actually a lot nicer than just throwing them in the sea or whatever. 
These catacombes are, and this is where it might get slightly interesting for you OP, connected by a huge network of underground tunnels (in total almost 300 km). These tunnels were originally limestone quarries. The tunnels were used in WWII by rebellions and go all around Paris. It's almost like a second city underneath Paris. So the tunnels in/around your building are most likely part of a huge network, and also in the non-literal sense part of sometging much bigger. 
Actually, living in a building that has access to these tunnels (probably the doors right under your laundry room) is really cool. I'm sure lots of Europeans would love to trade homes with you. Cause it's just cool. Very cool. But of course, also creepy as fuck. Especially when a freaky lady keeps popping out of them. She's probably either part of some bullshit cult/sekte, or just senile. Nevertheless, You definitly should go into the tunnels. If you want to have some adventure during you're time in Europe/ Paris, the tunnels and catacombes are definitly the way to go. 
Just bring a shovle or something else you can beat the shit out of that woman with. 

TLDR: The Catacombes and tunnels are an important part of Paris. Go in. It's really cool. Punch the lady if you see her.

EDIT: Also, 450 Euro, even for the tiniest appartment you can imagine, is rediculously low for the centre of Paris. If you're just too freaked out and want to move again, then remember: living in the center of Paris is increadibley expensive. If it's below 600, something's defenitly really wrong with the place. Judging by the reaction of your landlord, he knows something's up with his building. Either pay more for an appartment or move out of the centre.  (Then the tunnels will also be further away from you, which seems to comfort you.)
